item.title: One Crew Member Dies as Diesel Tanker Sinks off Ibiza
item.description: One crew member died as a tanker carrying diesel sank off the coast of Ibiza in the early hours on Thursday, local emergency services and authorities said. The Balearic Islands emergency service has activated an emergency plan after the diesel-carrying vessel sank about 25 nautical miles north of Ibiza, the emergency agency said on Thursday. Seven of the tanker’s 17 crew members were taken to Ibiza, but one of them was pronounced dead later in a hospital, the Balearic Islands emergency service…

item.title: Dutch Gas Network Operator Proposes Creation of Strategic Reserve
item.description: Gasunie, the Dutch gas network operator, has urged the Netherlands to create a strategic gas reserve to boost energy security amid international supply disruptions. The Netherlands remains vulnerable to external supply shocks, Gasunie said on Thursday as gas demand for heating is soaring in an early cold spell in most of Europe this week. There is no immediate risk of supply shortage, but the country, as well as the whole of Europe, remains vulnerable to gas supply shocks, the company said…

item.title: Oil Prices Rebound as Middle East Supply Fears Return
item.description: January WTI crude oil futures recovered from a three-month low this week as renewed concern over Middle East supply brought buyers back into the market. Prices had fallen early in the week as traders focused on the prospect of a global surplus. The selling slowed after WTI reached $79.07, and the market rallied Wednesday after Yemen’s Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura refinery. item.title: Iran Says LNG Carrier Exploded After Hitting a Mine in Hormuz
item.description: An LNG vessel has caught fire and exploded after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz during an attempt to transit on a route deemed “illegal” by Iran, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said in the latest communication of a tanker incident in the chokepoint. item.title: Turkmenistan Nears Major Milestone in $10 Billion TAPI Gas Pipeline
item.description: Turkmenistan expects a key section of a pipeline to begin supplying gas to Afghanistan’s third-largest city in early 2027, despite years of delays and hurdles in the $10-billion Turkmenistan–Afghanistan–Pakistan–India (TAPI) project, Turkmen officials have told Reuters. Turkmenistan is estimated to be the world’s fifth-largest holder of natural gas reserves, after Russia, Iran, Qatar, and the United States.
